chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Abū al-Jawzāʾ al-Munabbih ibn ʿAbd Allah, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:

If a man dies while traveling among women, and his wife is not among them, nor any woman related to him within maḥram kinship, he said: they should wrap him from the waist to the knees, and pour water over him by pouring, and they should not look at his ʿawrah, nor touch him with their hands, and they should purify him. And if women who are maḥram relatives are with him, they should wrap him, pour water over him by pouring, and touch his body, but they should not touch his private part.

key_terms.الرُّكْبَتَيْنِ: the two knees; the limit to which the covering is applied
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel; the circumstance in which this ruling applies
key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a person within unmarriageable kinship relations
key_terms.عَوْرَتِهِ: his intimate area that must not be viewed
key_terms.يُؤَزِّرْنَهُ: they should cover or wrap his lower body
key_terms.يُطَهِّرْنَهُ: they should purify him; meaning perform the required cleansing

ai.seo_question: How should a deceased man be washed if he dies in travel and only women are present?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling for washing a deceased man when only women are present during travel. It distinguishes between unrelated women and women who are maḥram relatives, permitting greater contact for the latter while maintaining the prohibition on touching the private part.
